title: Computationally validated CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing of the acetolactate synthase gene for herbicide resistance in tomato (Solanum lycopersicum Mill.)
author: Sunil Hajare
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.title: Design ALS guide RNA
steps.instruction: Design a 19‑nt gRNA targeting the conserved catalytic domain in exon 2 of the tomato ALS gene and validate it with CHOPCHOP v3 (score 97.6) and CRISPOR (score 94/97), confirming zero perfect‑match off‑targets in the genome.

steps.title: Prepare regeneration medium
steps.instruction: Prepare Murashige and Skoog (MS) medium supplemented with 2.5 mg L⁻¹ 6‑benzylaminopurine (BAP) and 0.5 mg L⁻¹ α‑naphthaleneacetic acid (NAA) for cotyledon explant culture; this formulation gave the highest shoot regeneration frequency of 59.78 %.

steps.title: Agrobacterium transformation
steps.instruction: Transform cotyledon explants by Agrobacterium‑mediated delivery of a CRISPR/Cas9 binary vector carrying the validated ALS‑specific gRNA.

steps.title: Select hygromycin‑resistant lines
steps.instruction: Place transformed explants on hygromycin selection medium; obtain twenty‑one putative transgenic lines.

steps.title: PCR confirmation of transgenes
steps.instruction: Screen T₀ plants by PCR for the presence of both Cas9 and gRNA cassettes; twelve lines were confirmed positive.

steps.title: Sequence ALS locus
steps.instruction: Amplify and sequence the targeted ALS region in the confirmed T₀ plants; identify site‑specific A→G transitions and A→C transversions located 15 bp downstream of the PAM, yielding a mutation efficiency of 19.05 % (4/21 edited lines).
